sections.title: On strongly pseudoconvex Kähler--Berwald manifolds
sections.abstract: The authors identify Kähler--Finsler metrics with Kähler--Berwald metrics and derive decomposition, uniformization, and rigidity results in the strongly pseudoconvex complex-Finsler setting.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and Theorem 1.5 state that every Kähler--Finsler metric in the paper's complex-Finsler framework is Kähler--Berwald; the authors also claim de Rham decomposition, uniformization, and Kobayashi/Carathéodory rigidity results.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metrics on complex manifolds; the decomposition results use Kähler--Berwald hypotheses, with the global decomposition stated for simply connected, complete manifolds.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed stronger-than-weakly-Kähler--Finsler condition is shown equivalent to the weak condition in complex dimension two; the paper's Carathéodory-metric rigidity statement also requires simple connectivity.

sections.title: $C^{0}$ stability of torsion-free $G_{2}$ structures along the Laplacian flow
sections.abstract: The authors prove dynamical stability of torsion-free $G_{2}$ structures under the Laplacian flow for closed structures initially in a $C^{0}$-neighborhood.
sections.claimed_result: For a compact 7-manifold with a torsion-free reference $G_{2}$ structure, Theorem 1.2 claims that sufficiently $C^{0}$-close closed initial structures in its cohomology class yield a global Laplacian-flow solution converging smoothly, modulo diffeomorphism, to a torsion-free structure.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact 7-dimensional manifold, torsion-free reference structure, closed initial $G_{2}$ structure in the reference cohomology class, and sufficiently small $C^{0}$ distance; the proof first establishes estimates for the Laplacian--DeTurck flow.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a local stability theorem near a torsion-free structure, not a long-time existence result for arbitrary initial data.

sections.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
sections.abstract: The paper develops an equivariant Chiu--Tamarkin complex, gives counterexamples to a symplectic-capacity product formula, and proves a Weyl law for toric domains.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct an uncountable family where their equivariant Chiu--Tamarkin capacities violate the proposed product equality, including a smooth concave toric domain in dimension six times a disk, and prove a Weyl law for all toric domains in $2n$-dimensional space.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Capacities are defined via the $S^{1}$-equivariant Chiu--Tamarkin complex; the explicit counterexample uses a concave toric domain of dimension at least six and a two-dimensional disk. Their introduction gives the Weyl-law bounds for open toric domains.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexample is for the capacities constructed in this paper; it does not by itself settle every related product conjecture for Ekeland--Hofer or Gutt--Hutchings capacities. Some product equalities require an additional homological condition.

sections.title: Ordering Is Not Deciding: Towards Preference-Consistent Multi-Objective Design--Decision Optimisation
sections.abstract: In constructed multi-objective problems, the authors show that Pareto filtering can discard the alternative with the best aggregate preference, while their IMAP method can select it from the full feasible set.
sections.claimed_result: Their examples show that Pareto optimality does not ensure a preference-consistent decision, because filtering may remove the aggregate-preference maximizer before preferences are applied; IMAP instead optimizes aggregate preference over the full feasible and acceptable set.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Constructed problems with two system performances, up to four preference functions, and up to two actors; the examples cover independent/interdependent performance relationships and monotone/non-monotone preferences.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is from small constructed instances, not a demonstration of performance on real-world design or group-decision problems.

sections.title: Frege's logic in Grundgesetze is nonclassical
sections.abstract: The author constructs a nonstandard model for Frege's subsystem without value-ranges and proves soundness and completeness for its first-order fragment under a new nonclassical semantics.
sections.claimed_result: The author says a nonstandard model confirms Landini's conjecture that a particular implication about Frege's horizontal is not provable in the subsystem, then establishes soundness and completeness for the first-order fragment with respect to boolean-truncation semantics.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns the subsystem of Grundgesetze without value-ranges and its first-order fragment, not the full formal system with value-ranges.
sections.unique_caveat: The change in semantics is established for that restricted fragment; it does not show that every part of Grundgesetze is nonclassical in the same sense.

sections.title: Canonical activation patterns and ReLU pattern varieties
sections.abstract: For unbiased ReLU networks, the authors relate activation-pattern combinatorics to algebraic varieties, characterize shallow-network stability, and give dimension results.
sections.claimed_result: For shallow unbiased networks, the paper characterizes pattern stability by linear independence of every set of min(n0,n1) first-layer rows; under a connected wall-graph condition it gives generators for the pattern variety's defining ideal, and relates functional dimension to variety dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Networks have no biases; the exact stability equivalence is for shallow architectures. The explicit ideal description requires the wall graph to be connected and to contain an edge for each neuron label.
sections.unique_caveat: For deeper networks the paper proves generic pattern stability, not generic combinatorial stability; the authors identify the latter as an unresolved step, especially for extending the analysis to biased networks.

sections.title: Continuous-Time Stochastic Contraction Induced by Common White Noise
sections.abstract: For Itô stochastic differential equations driven by common noise, the authors give differential characterizations of moment and almost-sure contraction in Finsler distances.
sections.claimed_result: Under the paper's mild hypotheses, the authors characterize Lp-contraction and almost-sure exponential contraction by necessary-and-sufficient differential conditions, relate them to incremental input-to-state stability, and apply the theory to noise-induced synchronization.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Itô SDEs with two trajectories driven by the same noise process; distance is measured using Finsler metrics, including Riemannian and norm-induced cases.
sections.unique_caveat: The criteria apply under the stated regularity hypotheses and to common-noise dynamics; the synchronization example does not establish robustness for arbitrary noise models.

sections.title: Nondoubling Calderón-Zygmund theory across geometries
sections.abstract: The authors build Calderón--Zygmund and Hardy/BMO theory for measure spaces without doubling, metric, or martingale structure, then apply it to flow trees.
sections.claimed_result: A stopping-time decomposition yields atomic Hardy and BMO spaces, duality/interpolation, and weak-type (1,1) and Hardy-space bounds; on arbitrary flow trees they derive endpoint bounds for Riesz transforms and spectral multipliers.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The space has an exhausting family of admissible sets with recursive child partitions; operator bounds assume a Hörmander condition and size control between stopping sets and their parents. The spectral-multiplier result requires a scale-invariant Sobolev condition of order greater than 3/2.
sections.unique_caveat: This is not a theorem for arbitrary singular-integral operators on arbitrary measure spaces: the recursive partition and operator hypotheses are essential.

sections.title: Uniform Positivity of the $F$-Signature and Pure Descent of klt Singularities
sections.abstract: The authors relate klt-type singularities to uniform positive lower bounds for the $F$-signatures of their reductions modulo sufficiently large primes, and apply this to pure descent.
sections.claimed_result: The authors affirmatively answer a uniform-positivity question and prove a converse: klt-type singularities have uniformly positive $F$-signature for reductions modulo all sufficiently large primes, while such a uniform lower bound for a normal singularity implies it is of klt type. They also give a reduction-mod-$p$ proof of pure descent.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result compares singularities in characteristic zero-style algebraic geometry with their reductions modulo sufficiently large primes; the converse is stated for normal singularities with a positive uniform lower bound on those reductions.
sections.unique_caveat: The lower bound is asserted only for sufficiently large primes; the abstract does not provide a single explicit threshold or numerical bound applicable to every singularity.
